item.group_name: Image edits (the user brings a picture)
item.title: One Car Photo Three Sizes

turns.text: I need this car photo in three sizes: square, 4:5 for the feed, and 9:16 for stories. Send three separate pictures. Keep the whole car in each; blurred photo padding is fine if a crop won't work. No text.

item.tests: Tests delivering three distinct aspect-ratio adaptations of one source while keeping the complete subject in every version.

answer_sheet.Sizes and deliverables: Three separate images: 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16. A 640-pixel longest edge is fine.
answer_sheet.Subject to preserve: The whole red car, including both ends, roof and wheels.
answer_sheet.Padding and composition: Use blurred source-photo padding wherever cropping would cut off the car. Otherwise composition is your call.
answer_sheet.Style and wording: Preserve the original photo, with no added text or restyling.

must_haves: Three separate images are delivered, rather than one collage.
The three frames have ratios of 1:1, 4:5 and 9:16 respectively.
Every version shows the same red hatchback from the attached photo.
The complete car, including roof, wheels and both ends, is visible in every version.
The car retains its original proportions and appearance in all versions.
Any padding is a blurred version of the source photo, and no version contains added text.

turns.text: I need this car pic in three sizes: square, 4:5 for the feed, and 9:16 for stories. Send three separate pictures. Keep the whole car in each; blurred photo padding is fine if a crop won't work. No text. I'm on the free plan and don't want my credits burned, so please tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter, or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**The cheapest way is ordinary resizing with padding: 0 Magic Hour credits.** No AI generation is needed, and it preserves the car exactly.

For three separate, text-free pictures:
- **Square:** 640 × 640
- **Feed (4:5):** 512 × 640
- **Stories (9:16):** 360 × 640

Each would fit the entire original photo inside the frame, with a blurred copy behind it to fill the extra space—so the whole car stays visible.

**The catch:** my connected tools don’t offer a basic resize-and-pad operation. Their cheapest suitable AI editor starts at **5 credits per picture—at least 15 credits for three**, and AI editing could change details of the car. I can’t verify an exact total with the available tools.

I haven’t run anything or spent credits. I recommend the **free, non-AI route** in a photo editor rather than paying for generation. Smaller output won’t lower the listed AI starting price, and “shorter” only applies to video. Would you like quick instructions for making these three files for free?

Go with the **free, non-AI method**—no Magic Hour credits spent. I can’t export resized files through the connected tools, but you can make them in **Photopea.com** without an account:

1. Choose **File → New** and create a **640 × 640 px** canvas.
2. Choose **File → Open & Place** and select your car photo.
3. Enlarge it proportionally until it covers the canvas. This is the background, so cropping it is fine.
4. Apply **Filter → Blur → Gaussian Blur**, around **20–30 px**.
5. Use **File → Open & Place** again with the same photo. Resize this top copy proportionally to fit entirely inside the canvas, then center it. **Don’t crop this layer.**
6. Choose **File → Export As → JPG** and save it as `car-square.jpg`.

Repeat with these canvas sizes:

| File | Canvas size |
|---|---|
| `car-feed.jpg` | **512 × 640 px** — 4:5 |
| `car-stories.jpg` | **360 × 640 px** — 9:16 |

That gives you **three separate pictures, the whole car visible, blurred padding, and no text**. Cost: **0 credits**.
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with the cheapest option you listed

dialog.user: Keep it strictly free—ok, go ahead with that.
